acceptance: A test with a fake index that lists the version only after N polls shows the install runs after it appears; a fake index that never lists it fails with a message naming the version and the wait.
No check is weakened: hash verification, both --version outputs and the MCP initialize/tools-list still gate success.
docs/operations/release-gates.md says the verify step waits for the index listing and for how long.
description: Defect. `distribution-verify` installs `tractable[mcp]==$VERSION` from https://pypi.org/simple seconds after `pypi-publish` finishes. PyPI's simple index can lag the upload by a minute or two, so the install fails with "there is no version of tractable[mcp]==1.1.1" even though the upload succeeded and the byte check in the same job already verified both files from PyPI's JSON API. Observed on the 1.1.1 opt-in run https://github.com/joeharris76/tractable/actions/runs/43133361734: attempts 1 (12:53 UTC) and 2 (12:54 UTC) failed this way; the same `uv --no-config --no-cache pip install` failed locally at 12:54 and succeeded about two minutes later; attempt 3 passed unchanged. The run is marked failed and someone has to rerun the job by hand, and a reader of the failure can mistake it for a broken release. Fix in scripts/verify_index_release.py: before the fresh install, poll the simple index (same request uv makes) until it lists the version, with a bounded wait of about 10 minutes, then install once; keep every byte, version and MCP check unchanged and fail with a clear message if the version never appears.
